value.title: embed-cap-heal — the provider's cap rejection becomes a re-split signal
value.summary: Close backlog row 117: inputs denser than the bytes/3 estimate slip under the chunk window unsplit and are rejected by the provider at 8192 tokens, then retried into permanent failure. Make the rejection a SIGNAL that re-splits the offending input, align chunk_plan's window with the FILL margin fit_to_cap already honours, and drain the five jobs stuck in prod.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Plan 009 shipped chunked embeddings and predicted this residual (impl-guide risk #2): estimate_tokens() is bytes/3, so content denser than ~2.55 chars/token — punctuation-heavy code, tool dumps, base64 — sits under the ~7,500-token window unsplit and the provider rejects it: `400 Invalid 'input[0]': maximum input length is 8192 tokens`. A retry re-sends the same bytes, so it fails forever. MEASURED IN PROD 2026-09-01/02: five embed jobs state=failed attempts=3 terminal=false — four `embed:git:github.com/AI-Substrate/pij:raw:…`, one `embed:conv:recovery:raw:c5a6be2d…` (a CONVERSATION turn). Largest observed item 20,872 chars → bytes/3 says ~6,957 tokens, real >8,192. A peer government (harness-engineering) is holding a ~250-seat conversation backfill until this lands, because every oversize turn in it would land silently in the same failed bucket. HYPOTHESIS TO VERIFY FIRST (not a fact): crates/core/src/tokens.rs already defines FILL=(2,3) so fit_to_cap effectively assumes 2 bytes/token, but 009's chunk_plan() (crates/daemon/src/enrich.rs) appears to size its window from estimate_tokens (3 bytes/token) without the FILL margin — if so, 20,872 chars would have been split by the margin alone, and aligning the window is the cheap half of the fix. The self-heal is the half that survives content denser than any constant.

sections.name: goals
value: A provider cap rejection never becomes a permanent failure for a splittable input: the offending item is identified, re-split tighter, and re-issued, bounded by a fixed number of rounds.
When the bound is exhausted, the job fails with a message naming the item, its byte length, and the ratio reached — never a bare provider echo.

chunk_plan's window honours the same FILL margin as fit_to_cap, so the common dense case never reaches the heal path; the chunk-count cost of that alignment is MEASURED on the fixture corpus and reported, not guessed.
The five jobs stuck in prod complete (or fail with a named reason) after deploy, with before/after evidence read from `flowspace3 status` and the jobs table.
Search over previously-failed content works: a turn from the recovered conversation job is findable by `flowspace3 search`.

sections.name: non_goals
value: No tokenizer dependency (option b of row 117) — the module's own rationale for an estimate stands.
No change to TOKEN_BUDGET, batch sizing, or the sub-batching f-001 added, beyond what re-issuing a re-split item needs.
No CLI changes; no conversation-ingest changes; nothing in crates/cli.
No change to the 8192 cap constants or the provider adapters' wire shapes — only their error CLASSIFICATION (cap-rejection must be distinguishable from other 400s).

value.claim: Alignment measured: the coder reports, from the fixture corpus, the chunk count before and after chunk_plan honours FILL, and states whether the 20,872-char prod item would have been split by alignment alone. This is a measurement, not a pass/fail — its receipt is the two numbers.
value.receipt: cargo test -p fs3-daemon chunk_plan -- --nocapture: ruled corpus 7→10, 33→50, 1→2; total 41→62; 20,872-byte item splits by alignment alone

value.claim: Self-heal, mutation-checked: a fixture input whose real token count exceeds the cap at the assumed ratio (a fake provider that counts tokens denser than bytes/3 and rejects with the cap error) is re-split and embedded as N>1 chunks; the SAME test fails without the heal (job reaches permanent failure). The PR body states the mutation.
value.receipt: cap_rejection_heals_dense_input_into_unique_chunks passed; removing the Error::InputTooLong heal arm made the same test fail 0/1 with the original cap rejection; arm restored and full cap_rejection_ set passed 3/3

value.claim: Bounded and named: with the re-split rounds exhausted (fake provider rejecting at every ratio), the job fails once with a message containing the item identity, byte length, and the final ratio; it is marked terminal so the boot sweep does not revive it. Asserted by test.
value.receipt: cap_rejection_exhaustion_is_terminal_and_named passed: one failed job; message contains source hash, 20872 bytes, final ratio 1 byte/token; terminal=true; requeue_failed sweep affected 0

value.claim: Classification is exact: only the provider's cap rejection triggers the heal; a different 400 (e.g. bad request body) still fails as before. Asserted by test on both openai and azure_openai adapters.
value.receipt: cargo test -p fs3-providers cap_rejection: 4 passed; OpenAI and Azure cap 400s map to Error::InputTooLong with input index; unrelated 400 controls remain Error::Provider

value.claim: PROD DRAIN (o-prime applies the bounce; coder provides the queries and reads them back with o-prime): before deploy `flowspace3 status --json` shows embed failed count=5; after deploy + bounce the five dedupe_keys (recorded in the receipt) are done or terminal-with-reason; `flowspace3 status` shows embed failed=0 or the named residue. Receipt = both status envelopes and the five keys' final states.
value.receipt: PRE-BOUNCE: flowspace3 status --json embed failed=5. Rows: 1314967=8ecded…, 1315244=9dce39…, 1316706=043365…, 1323215=043365… duplicate, 1344012=conv c5a6be2d; all failed attempts=3 terminal=false. NAMED PRECONDITION: requeue_failed collides on jobs_live_dedupe_idx unless duplicate jobs 1316706/1323215 are repaired first. O-prime owns the Jordan-approved prod repair at bounce. Automatic mechanism after repair: boot.rs:176-194 -> jobs.rs:506-534.

value.claim: REAL USAGE: after the drain, `flowspace3 search --source conversation "<a phrase from the recovered turn>"` returns a hit from conv job c5a6be2d's conversation, proving the healed content is searchable, not just stored. Receipt = the search envelope with the hit address.

value.title: Phase 1: heal + align + drain
value.brief: Single unit, single coder, no PM: (1) verify the FILL-alignment hypothesis and measure it; (2) classify cap rejection in both provider adapters; (3) re-split-on-rejection with a bounded round count and a named terminal failure; (4) tests incl. the mutation check; (5) PR; (6) drain evidence after o-prime's bounce.
